definitions.gloss: to hit it off, to get along instantly
definitions.explanation: A four-character idiom describing the instant rapport and mutual understanding that develops between people when they first meet.

examples.japanese: {初対面|しょたいめん}で{意気投合|いきとうごう}した。
examples.english: We hit it off at first meeting.

examples.japanese: {趣味|しゅみ}が{同|おな}じで{意気投合|いきとうごう}した。
examples.english: We bonded over having the same hobbies.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{意気投合|いきとうごう}して{一緒|いっしょ}に{事業|じぎょう}を{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The two hit it off and started a business together.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}らはすぐに{意気投合|いきとうごう}して{親友|しんゆう}になった。
examples.english: They immediately hit it off and became best friends.

notes:
FOUR-CHARACTER IDIOM ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご})

LITERAL MEANING: {意気|いき} (spirit, will) + {投合|とうごう} (to come together, to harmonize) = Spirits coming together in harmony.

USAGE PATTERNS:
・{意気投合|いきとうごう}する (to hit it off)
・{意気投合|いきとうごう}して＋verb (after hitting it off, ~)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{初対面|しょたいめん}で{意気投合|いきとうごう}する (to hit it off at first meeting)
・すぐに{意気投合|いきとうごう}する (to immediately get along)
・{意気投合|いきとうごう}して{友達|ともだち}になる (to become friends after hitting it off)

NUANCE: Always positive, describing a natural and mutual connection between people.

ENGLISH EQUIVALENTS:
・To hit it off
・To click
・To connect immediately

RELATED TERMS:
・{馬|うま}が{合|あ}う - to get along well (literally: horses match)
・{気|き}が{合|あ}う - to be compatible, to get along
・{仲良|なかよ}くなる - to become close/friendly
